title: Xanthe and the Sigil
premise: Jonah Okafor has spent her life as the invisible keeper of a sealed mountain gate, until the old gods of Thornfell begin answering prayers again and the sigil burned into her palm starts to glow. She learns she is the last heir of the gate's original builders, and that the god stirring beneath the mountain holds the soul of her brother Tam, sold to the court beneath in exchange for the family's long prosperity. As the moon wanes toward its thirteenth turn, Jonah must descend through smugglers' roads and god-haunted darks, bargaining with powers that feed on names, to steal Tam's soul back before the gate opens for good. In the end she succeeds only by surrendering her own name to the court, becoming the new keeper bound beneath the mountain—until Tam, restored above, finds a way to call her home.
about_author: T. M. Fairweather is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent six years mapping remote mountain passes before turning to fiction. They write fantasy rooted in folklore about borders, bargains, and the people who guard the doors everyone else forgets exist.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Nothing
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Establishes her quiet life tending the sealed Thornfell gate: checking wards, trading with smugglers, avoiding the village that half-remembers her family. Emotional beat: contentment built on deliberate invisibility, undercut by loneliness.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A dying shepherd's desperate prayer at the gate is answered by something on the other side; the ward-stones warm for the first time in decades. Jonah realizes the seal is thinning. Emotional beat: dread replacing routine.

chapters.title: The Sigil Wakes
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The birthmark on her palm burns and takes the shape of an intricate sigil matching the gate's carvings. The village priestess recognizes it and calls her 'daughter of the builders.' Emotional beat: identity forcibly revealed.

chapters.title: What Mother Buried
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, with a flashback to childhood. Searching her late mother's things, Jonah finds a ledger recording payments made every thirteen years—and a page torn out where her brother Tam's name should be. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Priestess Sef's POV. Sef explains the covenant: the family sold a soul to the court beneath the mountain to keep the gate shut, and the thirteenth moon marks when the debt comes due. Emotional beat: terrible clarity; Jonah learns she was raised as collateral.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Road
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She hires smuggler Brannoc Vale, who knows the under-mountain roads, and they enter the Thornfell caves as the first moon turns. Emotional beat: reluctant partnership, first taste of the dark.

chapters.title: The Toll of Names
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A river-crossing spirit demands true names as toll; Jonah gives a false one and pays in blood instead, learning the court's rules. Emotional beat: cunning under pressure, cost made visible.

chapters.title: Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. First glimpse of the subterranean court—beautiful, hollow-eyed nobles who trade in souls like coin. Jonah sees Tam among them, smiling and wrong. Emotional beat: hope twisted by horror.

chapters.title: Brother, Stranger
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam, soul-bound but aware, warns Jonah to leave: the court knows she's coming and wants the heir's sigil. Emotional beat: love shadowed by betrayal he cannot help committing.

chapters.title: The Bargain Refused
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The court's Regent offers a trade: her sigil and inheritance for Tam's freedom. Jonah refuses, sensing the trap—the sigil is what keeps the gate shut. Emotional beat: defiance with no good options.

chapters.title: Moonfall Above
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. In the village, prayers multiply and small miracles turn cruel; the gods answering are hungry. Sef must decide whether to help Jonah or protect the flock. Emotional beat: faith fracturing.

chapters.title: Vale's Price
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Brannoc reveals he once sold his own daughter's soul to the court and has been guiding seekers ever since, hoping one succeeds. Emotional beat: guilt confessed, alliance deepened.

chapters.title: The Hollow Choir
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. To reach the soul-vault, Jonah must pass the choir of the unnamed—souls stripped of identity who try to sing hers away. She clings to memories of Tam. Emotional beat: terror of self-erasure.

chapters.title: Ledger of Debts
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. In the vault's antechamber she finds the original covenant and learns the truth: her mother didn't sell Tam—he volunteered, to spare Jonah, the true heir. Emotional beat: devastating reframe of family love.

chapters.title: Stealing Light
chapters.summary: Jonah and Brannoc's alternating POV. The heist: using the sigil to unseal the soul-vault while the court sleeps. They take Tam's soul-flame but trigger the alarm of bells made of bone. Emotional beat: triumph flipping to flight.

chapters.title: The Long Way Up
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Pursued through collapsing smugglers' roads, Brannoc stays behind to hold a door and is taken by the court. Emotional beat: sacrifice, survivor's guilt.

chapters.title: Twelfth Turn
chapters.summary: Tam's POV, waking soulless-but-restored at the gate. He doesn't know Jonah, and the returning gods press against the weakening seal. Emotional beat: rescue achieved, everything still lost.

chapters.title: The Gate Opens
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. On the twelfth night the gate breaks; the old god pours through, offering Jonah power to rule Thornfell if she kneels. She nearly accepts—power would let her fix everything. Emotional beat: corruption's seduction at its peak.

chapters.title: Name Given
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Climax begins: Jonah realizes only a willing soul can reseal the gate. She speaks her true name into the sigil and offers herself to the court beneath, trading herself for the world above. Emotional beat: self-sacrifice as authorship of identity.

chapters.title: Keeper Below
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The gate seals with Jonah inside; Tam, carrying her memories given in the bargain, becomes the keeper above. Emotional beat: inversion of their roles, grief with purpose.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Bell
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Months later, Tam uses the sigil's echo and Brannoc's stolen knowledge to call Jonah's name back up through the stone. Something answers from below. Emotional beat: hope earned, not given.

chapters.title: Xanthe Rising
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah climbs out of the opened gate at dawn, renamed Xanthe by the court yet keeping the self she chose underground; the gods, fed on her refusal rather than obedience, withdraw. Brother and keeper stand together as equals. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed, inheritance transformed into choice.
